statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low at 12% while stress is elevated at 55%, reflecting a fourth consecutive Nasdaq-100 lower close set against an overnight futures session that has recovered 0.41% inside a contained, two-sided band with Treasury yields marginally lower and VIX easing.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD across the full 24-hour horizon. Conditional risk is concentrated in two structural checkpoints: the 13:30 UTC cash open together with the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI, published as the narrow 13:00-14:00 UTC danger window, and the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour in which August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close. headline: Overnight recovery inside a contained band keeps Nasdaq-100 mean reversion intact after a fourth lower close, with the cash open, a flash PMI and monthly expiration as the day's checkpoints
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,213.17 on 20 August, down 0.72% and roughly 2.5% on the week, a fourth consecutive lower close. The decline has been a grind rather than a rout: the session traded between 29,378.81 and 29,118.07 and closed about 95 points above its low, so retracements have remained available throughout the drawdown. Overnight, NQ futures have recovered to 29,419.25, up 0.41% against the 29,300.50 prior close, inside a two-sided band of roughly 29,274 to 29,433. The move is a drift toward the upper end of that band rather than the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that would threaten mean reversion, and no failed retracement has been observed.

The long end of the Treasury curve remains the driver of the weekly decline, but it is stabilising at the time of this assessment. The 10-year trades near 4.70%, the 2-year near 4.19% and the 30-year near 5.24%, each marginally lower on the day after Thursday reversed the relief that followed the Treasury's 19 August announcement that it would at least double long-end liquidity-support buybacks to at least $4 billion per operation from 9 September. Official H.15 data through 19 August put the 2-year at 4.19%, the 10-year at 4.65% and the 30-year at 5.19%. Volatility is elevated but decaying: VIX is 15.82, down 1.19% from its 16.01 close, and delayed cross-asset context shows VIX futures easing, gold firmer and long-bond futures only marginally soft.

Energy remains the second macro overhang. WTI trades near $86.24, down 0.68% on the day but up roughly 6% on the week, with Brent above $93, driven by the escalation of US sanctions policy toward Iran and a Strait of Hormuz that remains shut. That is a persistent stress input rather than a new discontinuity, and it has not so far transmitted into one-way Nasdaq-100 structure.

Breadth is conflicting rather than aligned. In the latest session seven of eight tracked megacaps closed lower with a mean change of about -0.9%, led by Amazon, Apple and Tesla, while four of seven tracked semiconductors closed higher with Micron up almost 4%. Conflicting breadth of this kind raises uncertainty and stress rather than tail. Today's scheduled structure is light: the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC is the only meaningful US release, and August monthly options expiration settles into the 20:00 UTC cash close. Next week carries the heavier stack, with GDP and Core PCE together on 26 August, a major semiconductor earnings call the same evening, and the Jackson Hole symposium opening on 27 August, whose keynote falls beyond both this forecast horizon and the seven-day event window published here.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-two of the 24 preceding clock-hours have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable with null assessment fields; no past opinion is reconstructed from later information. The two available slots are 2026-08-21T01:00:00Z, from the assessment generated at 01:34:51Z, which published tail 12%, stress 59%, confidence 83% and a mixed dominant mode, and 2026-08-21T06:00:00Z, from the assessment generated at 06:35:00Z, which published tail 12%, stress 57%, confidence 84% and a mixed dominant mode. Tail has been stable at 12% across both, while stress has stepped down as long-end yields stabilised. For context established from independent research rather than provider history, the Nasdaq-100 declined on each of 17, 18, 19 and 20 August and the 20 August session closed about 95 points above its low, so retracements remained available through the entire drawdown.
outlookSummary: The horizon runs from the current European pre-open through a full European and US session and then ends inside the weekend futures halt. Early European hours are scored at low tail risk on the contained, two-sided overnight band. Conditional risk rises into the US pre-market and peaks in the 13:00-14:00 UTC hour, which contains both the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMI and is published as the narrow danger window. A second, slightly lower peak falls on the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where August monthly options expiration settles into the cash close alongside weekend risk reduction. Every hour of the horizon maps to EA_ON, because none of the published tail scores reaches the block threshold. From the 21:00 UTC CME halt onward the scores are held flat and low: no continuous price path exists over the weekend, so accumulating headline risk is carried as gap risk into a Sunday reopen that falls outside this horizon. Confidence decays steadily across the closed hours as the evidence base ages.
